key_insight: A stabilized multi-mode Rheological Universal Differential Equation (mmRUDE) framework makes data-driven constitutive modeling more reliable by enforcing thermodynamic admissibility, improving training stability, and preserving interpretability.
engineering_relevance: The method can produce robust, extrapolatable rheological models for polymer processing and CFD simulations, especially for materials with broad relaxation spectra.
method: Log-compress input invariants to improve conditioning during training.
Use a split-network architecture to reduce stiffness and help learned corrections generalize.
Apply a differentiable projection layer to enforce the Clausius–Duhem inequality at every time step.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on LAOS data and then evaluated on unseen steady shear, transient stress growth, and extensional flows for both a synthetic multi-mode Giesekus case and an entangled silicone polymer melt.
watch_item: The framework adds algorithmic complexity, and the projection/stability machinery may require careful implementation and tuning for different constitutive datasets.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
